biography.value: Born in Sacramento, Xavier Becerra earned an economics degree and a law degree from Stanford University. He began his legal career in a legal-services office.

value: His campaign supports strengthening Medi-Cal and moving toward universal single-payer healthcare.
His campaign proposes treating housing as essential infrastructure, addressing price gouging and expanding help with childcare costs.
His campaign supports public investment in clean energy and grid resilience, and stronger disaster preparedness.

service.value: California Assembly member for one term, U.S. House member for 12 terms, and California Attorney General from January 2017 to March 2021.

biography.value: His campaign biography says he was born in London to Hungarian immigrants, attended Oxford, and worked in business, government and broadcasting before building businesses in California.

value: His current campaign proposes making the first $150,000 of income tax-free and applying an 8% flat tax above that amount, funded in part through spending reductions.
His campaign proposes reducing home-building costs and delays, including barriers to single-family housing.
His campaign supports phonics-based instruction, literacy and math proficiency, school accountability, and vocational training.
His campaign proposes abolishing the DMV as a standalone department and setting annual vehicle registration at $73.

service.value: His campaign biography reports that he served as a senior adviser to UK Prime Minister David Cameron and later taught at Stanford University.

value: His campaign prioritizes reducing living costs and growing jobs for working families.

His campaign emphasizes wildfire prevention, rebuilding and firefighter staffing.

contests.title: PROP 1 AUTHORIZES BONDS FOR HOUSING AFFORDABILITY PROGRAMS. LEGISLATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by the Legislature Authorizes $11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for housing affordability programs, including multifamily rental housing, mortgages for veterans, supportive housing, preservation of existing affordable housing, and downpayment assistance.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Increased state cost of $500 million to $600 million annually for about 25 years to repay the housing bond.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026

contests.title: PROP 2 INCREASES STATE’S RAINY DAY FUND. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by the Legislature Increases California's Rainy Day Fund, approved by voters in 2014, to provide funding for education, health care, public safety, and other essential services during economic downturns.

fiscalAnalysis.value: State budget reserves would be higher.

contests.title: PROP 3 PROVIDES PERMANENT FUNDING FOR SCHOOLS AND HEALTH CARE BY EXTENDING EXISTING TAX ON HIGH INCOMES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Makes permanent existing voter-approved tax rates for individuals earning over $371,000 (adjusted annually for inflation). Allocates tax revenues to public education.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Maintains $5 billion to $15 billion of annual state income tax revenue by making a temporary tax increase on high-income earners permanent instead of letting it expire in 2031.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Provides permanent funding for schools and healthcare by extending existing tax on high incomes

contests.title: PROP 4 REPEALS PROHIBITION AGAINST PUBLIC FUNDING OF ELECTION CAMPAIGNS. LEGISLATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by the Legislature Repeals prohibition on state and local governments offering public funding of candidate election campaigns. Public funding programs may not use funds earmarked for education, transportation, or public safety.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Ongoing costs to the state of a few hundred thousand dollars each year for the Fair Political Practices Commission to answer questions from state and local governments about public campaign finance programs.

contests.title: PROP 5 CHANGES RECALL ELECTION PROCESS FOR STATEWIDE OFFICERS. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by the Legislature Under current law, voters elect replacement candidates at the same time as the recall election. This measure instead fills recall vacancies by subsequent special election or appointment.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Net fiscal effect unknown. In the event of a recall, savings or costs of millions of dollars to administer the election depending on the office recalled.

contests.title: PROP 37 CREATES LOAN PROGRAM FOR MIDDLE-INCOME BUYERS OF QUALIFIED NEW HOMES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Authorizes $25 billion in bonds to offer eligible buyers fixed-rate mortgages for up to 17% of purchase price of a newly constructed home priced below about $1.5 million. Borrowers must be California residents, occupy the home, meet income limits, and pay at least 3% down. Bonds repaid by mortgage payments, not State.

fiscalAnalysis.value: No direct state or local costs.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Creates loan program for middle-income buyers of qualified new homes

contests.title: PROP 38 AUTHORIZES BONDS FOR IMMUNOLOGY MEDICAL RESEARCH. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Authorizes $8.4 billion in general obligation bonds for immunology and immunotherapy research, half to a single University of California-affiliated nonprofit medical research institute, half to research grants.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Increased state cost of $500 million to $600 million annually for about 20 years to repay the research bond, with some or all of the cost offset if the funded research generates revenue.

contests.title: PROP 39 PROHIBITS CITIZENS FROM VOTING UNLESS THEY PRESENT GOVERNMENT-ISSUED IDENTIFICATION. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Invalidates mail ballots that do not have last four digits of designated government-issued identification number written on envelope. Prohibits in-person voting without presenting government-issued identification.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Costs of between tens of millions of dollars and low hundreds of millions of dollars each year to implement new voting requirements.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Establishes additional voter identification and citizenship verification requirements

contests.title: PROP 40 IMPOSES ONE-TIME TAX ON CERTAIN TAXPAYERS. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT AND STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Imposes 5% tax on certain taxpayers with assets over $1 billion; revenue primarily for health care. Exempts revenues from constitutional requirements for school funding and spending limit.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Temporary revenue increase of tens of billions of dollars spread over several years from wealth tax on billionaires. Possible ongoing decrease of less than $1 billion per year in income tax revenue from billionaires.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Imposes one-time tax on certain individuals and trusts

contests.title: PROP 41 PROHIBITS NEW STATE TAXES THAT EXCLUDE REVENUES FROM STATE SPENDING LIMIT. REQUIRES AUDITS FOR NEW STATE SPECIAL TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Nullifies state taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that exempt their revenues from voter-approved state spending limit. Requires pre-election and recurring audits of programs funded by new special taxes.

fiscalAnalysis.value: The net fiscal effect is unknown as it depends on future decisions by voters, the Legislature, and other policymakers.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Requires audits of programs funded by new state special taxes

contests.title: PROP 42 PROHIBITS NEW STATE PERSONAL PROPERTY TAXES AND CERTAIN RETROACTIVE STATE TAXES. INITIATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Prohibits any new state tax (1) imposed on the ownership of personal property (all things people own other than real estate), or (2) that applies retroactively based on taxpayer’s past activities. Nullifies taxes enacted after January 1, 2026 that conflict with this measure.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Possibility that tax revenues will not go up as much in the future.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Prohibits new state personal property taxes and certain retroactive state taxes

contests.title: PROP 43 LIMITS VOTERS’ ABILITY TO RAISE REVENUES FOR LOCAL GOVERNMENT SERVICES. LEGISLATIVE CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENT.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by the Legislature Limits voters’ ability to pass voter-proposed local special taxes by increasing percentage of votes needed to approve such ballot measures from a majority (over 50%) to two-thirds, beginning January 1, 2027.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Possibility that local government tax revenues will not go up as much in the future due to a higher vote threshold for certain taxes.

contests.title: PROP 44 REQUIRES COMMUNITY HEALTH CLINICS SPEND 90% OF REVENUE ON PROGRAM SERVICES. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Imposes penalties on nonprofit Federally Qualified Health Centers (community clinics providing primary care to medically underserved areas and populations) that spend less than 90% of revenue on “program services” advancing their charitable purpose, including but not limited to patient services.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Increased state costs in the low tens of millions of dollars per year, covered by fees.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Requires community health clinics spend 90% of revenue on program services

contests.title: PROP 45 MODIFIES ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW FOR CERTAIN PROJECTS. INITIATIVE STATUTE.
contests.description: Put on the Ballot by Petition Signatures Amends California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) to expedite environmental review for certain projects (including most housing, transportation, water, and health projects) by setting deadlines to complete environmental review and resolve lawsuits challenging project approvals.

fiscalAnalysis.value: Initial costs for state and local governments, likely in the high tens of millions of dollars—potentially exceeding $100 million—annually, partly covered by fees. Uncertain, potentially more significant positive or negative longer-term fiscal effects.

measureIdentity.legacyTitle: Modifies environmental review for certain projects
